Front: Explain the distinct phases of the classloading process.
Back: Loading, Linking (Verification, Preparation, Resolution), and Initialization.
Extra: Why it matters: Understanding these phases helps debug static initialization ordering and linking errors. Gotcha: Static fields are preparation-initialized to defaults (0/null) before initialization runs.

Front: Explain the parent delegation model and how it works step-by-step.
Back: A ClassLoader delegates dynamic class loading to its parent classloader before searching itself.
Extra: Why it matters: Ensures core APIs cannot be shadowed or overridden by untrusted user libraries. Hierarchy: Bootstrap ClassLoader -> Platform ClassLoader -> Application ClassLoader -> Custom ClassLoaders.

Front: Explain why JVM classloaders partition class type namespaces.
Back: Class identity is a combination of fully-qualified name and defining ClassLoader instance.
Extra: Why it matters: Isolates webapps or plugins. Gotcha: You will get `ClassCastException` if you cast between instances loaded by different ClassLoaders, even if they have the exact same package and class names.

Front: Explain why and how Service Provider Interfaces (SPI) break parent delegation.
Back: Core APIs (Bootstrap loader) need to locate driver implementations in the application class loader.
Extra: Solution: Uses the Thread Context ClassLoader (TCCL) to gain downward visibility. By calling `Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader()`, core classes bypass the top-down parent delegation.

Front: Explain how dynamic classloading can cause Metaspace memory leaks.
Back: References to loaded class instances prevent their ClassLoader and loaded class metadata from being garbage collected.
Extra: Common gotcha: Leaving static references, ThreadLocal variables, or JDBC driver registrations pointing to application classes in a container prevents unloading the entire custom classloader, leaking native Metaspace memory.

Front: Explain the difference between `Class.forName` and `ClassLoader.loadClass` regarding class initialization.
Back: `Class.forName` initializes the class by default, while `ClassLoader.loadClass` only loads and links it.
Extra: Why it matters: Running static blocks can execute heavy setup operations. If you only want to inspect class metadata without running code, use `loadClass` or the three-argument overload `Class.forName(name, false, loader)`.

Front: Explain the differences between the Bootstrap ClassLoader and the Application ClassLoader.
Back: Bootstrap loads base core modules (like String, Object) and is native. Application loads user classpath code.
Extra: Why it matters: The Bootstrap loader is represented by `null` in Java API calls. Application ClassLoader is a Java subclass of `ClassLoader` accessible via `ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader()`.

Front: Explain how the Linking phase's Verification step contributes to JVM security.
Back: Validates class structure, stack maps, type rules, and instruction patterns to ensure safety.
Extra: Why it matters: Prevents malicious bytecode (e.g. modified class files trying to access private fields directly or stack-smash the virtual machine) from executing, throwing `VerifyError`.

Back: `ClassNotFoundException` is a checked exception. `NoClassDefFoundError` is an unrecoverable linkage error.
Extra: Difference: `ClassNotFoundException` occurs during dynamic reflection lookup (e.g. `Class.forName()`). `NoClassDefFoundError` occurs when a class was present during compilation but cannot be loaded at runtime during linking.

Front: Explain the JVM Metaspace sizing parameters and how it handles class metadata garbage collection.
Back: Metaspace is native memory allocated by OS. It is garbage collected only when its defining ClassLoader is collected.
Extra: Configuration: Use `-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize` to prevent Metaspace from consuming all system RAM. Classloader GC is atomic: either all loaded classes are garbage collected together, or none are.
